evidence.observation: H5 reads "when a model's redaction policy selects a verdict's roles, `message` becomes a fixed marker and `offending_facts` one marker row. A host of such a model sees which constraint failed and not the rows". At this checkout the disclosure mode decides redaction. docs/reference/disclosure.md:20 gives the default as "| unset | redacted unless `--unredacted` |". Line 210 lists `gnd verify` as "declared roles: shown under `internal`, redacted under `customer`". src/gnd/commands/verify.py:66 calls `_add_unredacted_argument(verify_parser)`. So outside `customer` mode a host of a redacting model can get the rows. docs/how-to/disclosure-mode.md already documents this, and it shows `offending_facts`, although H6 does not count that page.

§2 LR1 has the page say "what a redacting model hides (H5)", and R0.6 reads "**R0.6 One home per rule.**". Neither the LR1 steps nor the §5 citations name docs/reference/disclosure.md, `--unredacted`, `--disclosure internal` or `GND_DISCLOSURE`. The page would therefore restate a rule that already has a home, and would not tell a host how to get the rows it is allowed to see.

The plan authors "a redacting copy of" / "the reading model, and a derivation failure `(r3)`", and H2 copies "`reading_fixture/reading.orm.json` and its include `depth_fixture/vocabulary.orm.json`". The failing constraint `fact_types[subject_label].constraints[0]` is declared in vocabulary.orm.json, which reading.orm.json includes under a pinned sha256 (`25ac1974…`). src/gnd/redaction.py:97-106 reads `redact: true` from the fact type or role itself. A copy that edits only reading.orm.json therefore does not redact this verdict. The result also depends on the test process's GND_DISCLOSURE, which the plan does not pin.

concerns.recommendation: Extend H5 to cover the disclosure modes. Have the LR1 page cite docs/reference/disclosure.md and say that `--unredacted` or `--disclosure internal` shows the rows outside `customer` mode. Specify the redacting fixture as a vocabulary copy with `redact: true` on subject_label and a re-pinned include digest. Run the test with GND_DISCLOSURE unset and once under `internal`.
concerns.title: LR1's redaction case leaves out the disclosure mode that decides whether a host sees the rows

evidence.observation: D1 reads "(d) `(r3)` Reuse or extend the packaged regression corpus and its answer key (H24)", and §2 LR3 reads "and its answer key (H24), extended where the reading stages need".

R0.4 reads "adds a second fixture beside them and changes none." and §5 ends "LR3 adds a" / "fixture and changes none.". Extending the corpus changes an existing pinned fixture. tests/test_li1_assurance_report.py:7 says the expected outcomes "live in src/gnd/examples/literature/expected/ and were approved with the corpus", and src/gnd/examples/literature/answers/heldout.sha256 pins a held-out digest.

The LR3 lane is "`uv run pytest -q tests/test_lr3_reference_set.py tests/test_ld3_reading_workflow.py tests/test_ld4_revision.py tests/test_ld5_verdict.py --tb=short`". It leaves out tests/test_li1_assurance_report.py, tests/test_li3_diagnostics.py, tests/test_li4_assertions.py and tests/test_release_acceptance.py. All four reference the assurance scorer, the answer key or the regression corpus.

concerns.recommendation: Choose one. Either limit D1 (d) to reuse (a copy, or an additive overlay that leaves corpus/, answers/ and expected/ byte-identical), or amend R0.4 and §5 to allow a corpus change and add the li1, li3, li4 and release-acceptance tests to the LR3 lane. Record the choice under fix-lr3-existing-corpus in §11.

evidence.observation: LR2-C5 reads "the example's README says its verify document is the joined attempted sections with no sidecar", and §11 reads "the example verifies the joined attempted sections with no sidecar". In fact `_checked` (src/gnd/examples/literature/reading.py:274-286) writes `<stem>.population.extraction.json`, built by `_extraction_sidecar` (:258-265), which carries `document` and `document_sha256` for that document. It then verifies with `--artifacts bundle`. The example writes an extraction sidecar that binds the document by digest. It writes no anchor sidecar.

H9 reads "the document the example hands to `gnd verify` is the attempted sections of one pass joined with newlines, not the declared source and not one shown section". That is true for the broad and targeted passes (reading.py:391). For the reported conflict, which §3 makes LR1's main fixture, the document is `inputs.raw["conflict.txt"]` (reading.py:395).

concerns.recommendation: Make LR2-C5 and the README say 'no anchor sidecar' and state that the extraction sidecar binds the joined document by digest. Note that the reported conflict is verified against conflict.txt. The LR2 test then holds an accurate sentence.
concerns.title: LR2-C5 would have the README say 'no sidecar', though the example writes an extraction sidecar

evidence.observation: LR1-C3 reads "**LR1-C3** every field name the page's section uses, at report level or verdict level, is a property in `report.schema.json` and a key of the live report at that level; the test takes the names from the section's code spans `(r3)`".

r3 adds "are the `derivations` with `verdict: "fail"` (H23)" and "A failing derivation names itself by `derivation_ref`", followed by `findings`. In src/gnd/report.schema.json, `derivation_ref` and `findings` are properties of the `derivation_verdict*` definitions, not the constraint `verdict*` definitions (`verdict_v10` holds constraint_ref, offending_facts and the rest). The two packaged sources have no failing derivation. So 'verdict level' and 'the live report' do not say where these names are checked. The code spans that §2 models the section on also hold values (`"fail"`, `warning`, `uniqueness`), which are not field names.

concerns.recommendation: State LR1-C3 over three levels: report, constraint verdict and derivation verdict. Check each against its schema definition and against the live report of the fixture that carries it; derivation fields come from the authored derivation failure. Say how the test separates field names from values in code spans, for example with a listed set of names or a marked syntax.
concerns.title: LR1-C3 does not cover the derivation-verdict fields r3 adds to the page

criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, a phase cannot be specified, implemented and tested as the plan writes it, or the software would not demonstrably do what the plan claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

This is the second and final review round. The first round reviewed r2; its report is .gnd-planning/reviews/literature-reading-reference-r2-panel/PANEL-REVIEW.md (context only). Section 11 maps its seven fixes to sites in r3. For each fix, say whether r3 resolves it, and report any new inconsistency a fix introduced.
Rows tagged (o) (D6) and the owner rulings quoted in section 8 are owner rulings. Do not re-argue them; report only a ruling applied inconsistently or one that makes a criterion impossible.

For each phase LR1 to LR3, can it be specified, implemented and tested as sections 2 and 4 write it, with the lanes section 9 names, within the scope sections 2 and 7 state? LR3 is deliberately an outline that waits for literature-host-interfaces LH1 and LH2 and for owner rulings; judge whether that dependency and its gate are clear, not whether LR3 is fully specified.

Does each code location, line number, command result and quoted message cited in the plan (notably section 1, H1 to H25) match the repository at this checkout? Cite the plan line and name the source file and line in the observation.
Every concern's evidence must quote the plan file. The draft LR1 spec (notes/phase-LR1-spec.md), the milestone README and the first-round report are context only, not under review.
